message:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you so much for getting back to me!

Right now, we’re leaning toward digital printing, primarily for pareos and textile accessories. The broader aesthetic is refined, artisanal, and centred on luxury resort wear, with natural textures, woven influences, and imperfect detailing rather than anything overly polished or graphic.

I’ve attached the reference imagery to give you a clearer idea of the diagonal basket weave direction and the overall mood. We definitely want it to look organic and elevated rather than flat, with a strong textural quality.

IS it possible to enlarge these, or treat them as references, to develop an original textile print of our own? We’d also like to produce 2 x block colour pareos using the mustard / burgandy shades from the attached reference, along with the black border. However, we’re keen to get your help with the Zebra & woven print first.

We completely understand the timing as well. Quality is our priority, so we’d prefer to allow enough time for the final files to feel carefully considered and ready for production.

Let me know your thoughts

Thank you so much for sending the references and explaining the wider direction. It really helps me understand the world you’re creating.
The good news is that both ideas are achievable. The diagonal basket weave references provide exactly what I need as a starting point. My approach would be to construct the texture manually in Procreate, giving it the handmade and imperfect character you described: organic, artisanal, and elevated. I would then bring in the reference image as a texture overlay to capture that particular rattan grain within the illustration, allowing the finished print to retain the original feeling without simply enlarging a photograph. After that, I’d technically perfect the seamless repeat in Photoshop and Illustrator so the delivered file is production ready.
The zebra references are also very clear, and I love this direction! The bold, flowing stripes over the gold/camel base feel especially luxurious. I can develop this one with a freer, more gestural illustration style so it remains lively instead of looking flat.
Let’s begin with the zebra and basket weave! After both have been approved and you’re pleased with the direction, we can go directly into the block colour pareos.
For timing, I’d suggest 7 business days to complete both prints. I’d provide an intermediate check-in around day 3 or 4 so you can review the direction before receiving the final files. If adjustments are needed, my process includes 2 additional revision rounds from that point. I always try to keep the overall timeline as efficient as possible without rushing the detailed work!
I have one final question: do you know which fabric you’ll be printing onto? Silk, viscose, and cotton all require slightly different colour profiles for digital printing, and I’d like to ensure the CMYK files are calibrated for your particular supplier.
Really looking forward to this project!

I’m so glad I found you!!
Everything sounds great and feels completely in line with what we’re looking for. I especially love the plan to create the texture manually, as that will keep it feeling organic and elevated rather than too digital.

Let’s start with the zebra and basket weave, and once those are approved, we can continue with the block colour pareos. I can confirm the Pantone colours for you as well, although you may be able to identify them from the image.

The fabric will most likely be cotton voile, with silk/cotton voile also a possibility depending on the final sampling. I’ll confirm the exact fabrication with the supplier soon.

Really excited to see the first check-in!!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I’m so pleased we’re on the same page and really excited to bring the project to life!
Before beginning, I wanted to quickly clarify a few points so the process runs smoothly.
Regarding the Pantone colours, matching from photographs taken under ambient lighting isn’t completely dependable. I’ll therefore create my own visual approximation based on the references, then refine it once you’ve confirmed the exact Pantones with your supplier. This means we can get started without waiting for that information!
I also have a quick question about the basket weave: do you have an approximate size in mind for each diamond unit within the repeat? Even a rough measurement would help me establish the scale before constructing the tile.
For the fabric, voile cotton or silk/cotton voile will work very well for this direction. If your supplier can provide a specific ICC colour profile for the digital printer, I’d be very happy to receive it, as it will help me calibrate the CMYK files for their machine. If they don’t have one, that’s absolutely fine; I’ll use standard CMYK, and they can make any necessary adjustments themselves, which is entirely normal.
I’ve detailed the complete project scope in the attached document for you to review. When you have a moment, I’d also love for the contract to be activated on Upwork so we can officially get everything underway!
Very excited about this!
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Perfect, everything sounds great!
I completely understand the situation with the Pantones, and I’m happy for you to begin with a visual approximation before we refine it once production confirms the final Pantones. That approach makes complete sense.

For the basket weave, we’re imagining each diamond measuring roughly 5cm diagonally across the repeat. We’d also like a very very fine mustard edge outlining the woven detail.

For the zebra design, we’d like a black edge/border surrounding the print.
I’ve attached a PDF containing the mockups and some extra references for you to use as well!

I understand that your current quote covers the two patterns, so we can start with those before reviewing the additional designs afterward. However, could you confirm whether the other two block versions are also covered by this quote? I’ve included the Pantone colours for the terracotta and mustard shades we were hoping to use, so please let me know whether that’s possible for you.

I’ll also ask the supplier whether an ICC colour profile is available and forward it if they have one!! I’ll go onto Upwork and activate the contract shortly so we can officially begin.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! Thank you, the PDF is extremely useful! Having the basket weave scale reference and the Pantone colours gives me a much clearer foundation to work from.
The block colour pareos weren’t included in my initial quote. However, since we’re already developing the collection together and they’re relatively straightforward to execute, I’m happy to add them at no additional cost. I see that as part of making sure this first collection is done properly! This scope includes one scale variation for each colour. If you decide you’d like further variations after reviewing the results, we can arrange those as an add-on!
With the references, Pantone colours, and design information you’ve now supplied, I feel we have a very clear and complete brief. I’ll treat this as the confirmed scope covered by the quoted price, while any new elements or creative directions introduced later can be discussed as add-ons!
I’m looking forward to the contract being confirmed so I can get started!

You’re incredible, thank you so much!!
This is only the first capsule, so if everything aligns, we’d love to keep working with you on the next few as well. Would you be interested? I’ll confirm it now x

I’m so happy to hear that! I would absolutely love to keep collaborating on the upcoming capsules. Developing this collection thoughtfully from the outset is exactly the kind of work I enjoy most.
There’s just one small detail before you confirm: I noticed that the first milestone is currently dated May 22, which is tomorrow! Based on our conversation, the initial check-in would happen around 4 business days after we begin, so it may be worth changing that date to match the actual schedule. I simply want to ensure everything is clearly arranged from the start!
I’m so excited to begin!
Of course! I’ve updated it to Monday now. Is that okay? X
Great, Monday is perfect! I’m activating the contract now—let’s get started! 🌿

YAY! So excited. I’ll speak with you on Monday.
Have a lovely weekend x
Same to you—have a wonderful weekend! Speak on Monday

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]!
I’ve attached the Milestone 1 PDF containing every print developed to date. Below is an overview of what’s included and the information I need from you before continuing!
1\. Contents of this delivery
The Basket Weave print is provided in two texture treatments, Frottage and Reference-Based, with two scales for each. The Zebra print includes three directional options—Noir, Savanna, and Gold Skin—each presented both as a tile detail and at full repeat scale. There are also two block colour pareos, Rooibos Tea and Sudan Brown, each featuring two border scale choices, Slim and Full. For reference, every mockup is displayed at 110 x 180 cm.
You can review the full resolution repeat files here: [URL_001]
2\. Decisions needed from you
Which Zebra option do you prefer: 01 Noir, 02 Savanna, or 03 Gold Skin? For the Basket Weave, would you choose Frottage or Reference-Based? And for the block colour pareos, is the Slim or Full border scale more suitable for the collection? When reviewing, please refer to the measurements provided in the PDF, as they represent the true scale on fabric.
3\. Colour note: screen compared with fabric
The warmer golden shades, particularly in the Gold Skin zebra option, will look slightly more matte once printed on fabric than they do on screen. That is a normal result of pigment printing on voile rather than any reduction in quality; it is simply how the material displays colour. I wanted to clarify this before production to prevent any surprises!
4\. Information required before preparing final files
I need confirmation of your fabric supplier’s ICC profile so I can calibrate the CMYK files, along with the exact Pantone references confirmed by your supplier if available. I’ll also need the final seam allowance measurements to add to the digital production files, plus any further changes or comments regarding the chosen prints.
5\. Milestone 2 schedule
After receiving your selections and feedback, I’ll work toward May 29 as the Milestone 2 deadline. Should I complete the work sooner, I’ll deliver everything ahead of that date!
I’m looking forward to hearing what you think!
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
When you confirm that you’re satisfied with this delivery, I’ll officially submit Milestone 1 for approval on Upwork, allowing us to proceed with the final files!
I’ll send you a Google Form later today so your feedback can be gathered in a structured format, making revisions simpler for both of us!
Hi again! This is the feedback form I mentioned. It includes all the prints as well as the setup information I need before proceeding. Thank you! [URL_002]
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]! Tomorrow I’m going through the designs with my business’s partner, and then I’ll send you our feedback, mainly regarding the weave! I’ll get back to you tomorrow.
Hi! That’s perfect—take all the time you need! I’m looking forward to your feedback!

Hello again!
I spoke with Ella, my business partner, and we’ll be reviewing everything together over the weekend.

Would it be alright for us to send the amends on Monday? Please let me know whether that timing works.
I already have a few minor colour changes in mind. The Zebra currently feels a little too gold, and I’d love it to be lighter. For the weave, I prefer the 7.5cm option you showed, although I’d possibly like that lightened as well. It would also be helpful to see it with the border.
I’ve prepared my feedback, but I’d like to go through it with her first so everything is completely clear!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! Monday is absolutely fine! Once you’ve reviewed everything with Ella, the colour changes should be straightforward and quick to address. I just have one question about the weave border so I can follow the correct direction: every option I showed already includes a thin mustard border. Did you have something more noticeable or thicker in mind, or is the existing border right and the main change is simply making the colour lighter? You can include that clarification with your feedback on Monday! Speak soon!

Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Thank you for putting all of these options together. The direction is definitely moving closer, but I have several notes around colour \+ scale to make the result softer, more elevated, and more TELA MARE.

The references we provided were intended to evoke something tonal and naturally aged. At present, the artwork feels a little too clean and saturated, so we’d like to bring in additional softness, irregularity, and depth. The aim is for the prints to look collected and textural rather than excessively graphic.

In general, I think both designs need:
\* reduced contrast
\* additional grain
\* a stronger texture overlay
\* edges that are slightly more faded
\* less of a “perfect vector” appearance

Zebra print:
\* The zebra currently appears slightly too yellow/gold and has a little too much contrast.
\* I’d like the gold softened into more of a sandy caramel / soft bronze shade.
\* Overall, it should look vintage, costly, and sun-faded rather than bright or too golden.
\* The bigger, more organic stripe treatment feels like the strongest direction.

Weave print:
\* The current weave is leaning somewhat too orange/red.
\* I’d like to move it toward a softer brushed brown with greater depth and less warmth.
\* Our preferred scale is the larger 5cm diagonal weave, so ideally we would combine:
→ the tone/colour used in the smaller weave
→ with the 5cm version’s larger scale.

Across everything, the result can feel more tonal, softer, and more lived-in—less saturated and polished, and instead more earthy, natural, and collected.

I think we’ll be extremely close once the tones have been refined!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I’m very happy to hear the direction is getting closer, and thank you for providing such detailed feedback. It makes the process much easier and allows me to reach the right result more quickly!
Before starting the revisions, I’d like to confirm that I’m updating the exact files you selected. Could you either send a screenshot or provide the specific option name you want to develop further for each print, both the Zebra and the Weave? The option names appear in the PDF exactly as shown in the presentation. This will prevent any mix-up and ensure I work directly from your chosen versions!
A quick point regarding the requested grain and texture changes: the final files will reproduce the colour adjustments accurately. The digital preview will also provide a good representation of the grain and texture direction, but the fabric sample will ultimately determine the final appearance because pigment printing on voile absorbs some of that effect depending on the printer and the fabric tension. I just wanted to mention this before production so we share the same expectations!
Talk soon!
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
Ok fabulous!
Thank you so much

For the Weave: Gastaldon\_ Textil DBW Handcrafted Texture 5cm
(I also love the detailing visible in the attached screenshot that we originally shared as refence)
For the Zebra: Gastaldon\_Textil Zebra Savanna (I love this option, but would like it to be less yellow/gold)

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002],
I’ve just reviewed the Zebra designs together, and honestly, I like every one of them. I added a border, and that has made the designs feel even more resolved.
Could we see both the smaller and larger scale options with the tone reduced slightly? I’d really like to compare them side by side.
After looking again at the option on the left, I also really like the texture and gentle sheen you’ve achieved. It’s looking beautiful.
Please let me know whether that’s possible. I definitely feel that adding the border ties the whole design together?

Regarding the Weave Print:
We really love the handcrafted option you presented.
We definitely prefer the larger 5cm diamond scale.
If possible, we’d like to match the colour from the original reference.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! Perfect, I’ve already started working through the revisions! I can apply the colour adjustment to all three Zebra directions so you can compare them and decide which feels the most TELA MARE. The extra Weave references you provided are very useful and give me a precise direction to follow. I’ll share the revised options with you tomorrow!
Talk soon!
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I’ve been developing the revisions you requested across both prints. The high resolution files are available through the Drive link below so you can review them properly.
For the Zebra, I’m presenting three directions, each adjusted toward a softer caramel/bronze palette with lower contrast. They each retain a slightly different personality, allowing you to compare them and tell me which feels most TELA MARE, or whether you’d prefer to merge details from multiple options. For the Weave, I’ve included the revised colour direction developed from your reference. [URL_003] I’m looking forward to hearing your thoughts!
Talk soon,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! A quick update: I’ve added two more files to the Drive folder. These include a before-and-after comparison for the Weave, plus one additional Zebra direction where I developed the edges further. I wanted you to review those before sending your feedback.
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002],
These are beautiful—we love them. Thank you!
I think we can now proceed to the final artwork.
Could you add a small border around each design?
Zebra — Black border
Weave — Mustard border
Provided you’re happy with that, we can move on to the block print stage afterward.
Are you comfortable using the Pantone colours we chose?

EN INGLÉS
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I’m so pleased that you love the direction—it really means a lot!
For the finished artwork, I’ll work closely from your initial references to create the finish you envisioned. Before continuing, I have a few technical points to confirm so the files are delivered exactly as required:
1\. Zebra direction
Can you confirm that the Savanna version is the one we’re taking forward for the final artwork?
2\. Borders
I’m happy to apply borders to both designs. The updated files currently use a 1.5 cm border on both the Zebra and the Weave. Would you like to retain that size, or should it be changed?
On the block colour pareos, the Slim border measures approximately 7 cm, while the Full border is approximately 17 cm. Please confirm whether those measurements should remain or be modified before I proceed.
3\. Seam allowance
Can your supplier confirm how many centimetres they require for the seam allowance? The amount can differ according to the construction method and fabric. Once you provide it, I’ll incorporate it directly into the digital files so they are ready for cutting.
4\. Pantone colours
My initial work used the colour references you supplied, although the shades evolved slightly during revisions. In the final delivery, I’ll provide the exact CMYK values together with the nearest Pantone equivalents for every colour, giving your supplier all the necessary information.
After you confirm these details, I can prepare the final files and aim to deliver everything by June 10!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]

1\. Zebra Print - Our actual preference is the smaller-scale ZEBRA NOIR option: Gastaldon\_Textil ZebraNoir\_ Edited
2\. Borders - We’ve chosen NO BORDERS! Please remove every border so the print repeats easily, with the artwork extending fully to the edge. What you have already supplied is perfect.
3\. Yes, retain those measurements: 7cm thinner and 17cm + Seam allowance 1.5 cm, which will accommodate a rolled hem finish.
4\. Pantone colours - that works for us. Thank you so much!
Thank you! xx
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! Perfect! Now that I have those details, I’ll prepare the production-ready files and send you the Drive folder sometime between today and tomorrow!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! The link below contains the final delivery folder. Before you forward the files to your supplier, here is a brief summary of the contents and some important notes.
Inside the folder are the four production-ready pareo files, repeat tile files for Zebra Savanna and Diagonal Basket Weave, and a Technical Sheet listing all colour references and file specifications. A README is also included with a detailed explanation of everything in the folder.
Regarding the Basket Weave palette, the colours moved away from your initial reference during the revision stage so they would correspond more closely with the real woven texture you provided. The CMYK and Pantone values listed in the Technical Sheet relate to the final revised shades rather than the original palette. I’ve recorded this in the Technical Sheet notes so your supplier has the relevant context.
I’ve added the tiles as a bonus. Although they aren’t required for this production run, they may be useful if you later want to apply the designs to products other than pareos—anything suited to a repeating pattern.
The folder can be downloaded for 30 days and will remain available until 10/07/2026. Please download all contents before then.
[URL_004]

I look forward to hearing from you
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! Thank you so much for approving everything.
When the print samples arrive, I’d love to know how they turned out. If viewing the physical samples reveals that the colours need adjustment, I’m happy to provide one round of tweaks. Testing the print is a normal part of the process, and I want the final design to work beautifully on fabric rather than only looking right on screen.
Working with you on Tela Mare has been a genuine pleasure—thank you for trusting me with the first collection. I’m excited to see it produced, and I’d love to be involved again whenever you’re ready to begin the next one.
When the Upwork contract is closed, you’ll be asked to submit a review. It would mean a great deal to me while I continue developing my profile.
All the best,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002]
We’ve just spotted an error!
Tela Mare \_ 3 is also wrong. It needs to be reversed, with the black border and mustard inside.
Would you be able to correct this for me?
We’ll absolutely leave you an amazing review! At the moment, we’re just checking the scaling once more.
There shouldn’t be any additional changes, but if that’s okay, I’ll get back to you in 2 hours?xx
That’s no problem! I based my interpretation on the wording in your original reference, but I should have confirmed it with you when I was uncertain. I’ll correct it within half an hour!

The corrected file is now in the Drive folder, and I’ve revised the Technical Sheet as well. One important point regarding scale: because the files are raster-based and created from analogue illustrations, they can’t be enlarged very much without reducing quality. I wanted to make sure you had that information!

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], thank you for explaining!
We need to resize the artwork to 130cm x 170cm because the pareo was too long, which means 133 x 173cm once the seam allowance is included.
Can I resize the files you provided myself? Is that something I can do using a PDF?
Thank you so much!! xx

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! The files can be resized if you have the editable versions and suitable software. However, I’d recommend allowing me to do it so the dimensions remain exact and the artwork stays clean. I’m currently on vacation and will be back next week, so I’ll take care of it for you then!

You’re incredible, and I appreciate you so much
But only if you don’t mind xx

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! The rescaled files at 133 x 173cm are now in the Drive folder called "Resize". Just be aware that the Technical Sheet continues to display the old measurements — those can be changed easily using any PDF editor.
I also have one small request: Argentine tax regulations require me to provide an official export invoice for the work we’ve done together. Could you send me your full name, address (street, city, state, zip code) and email?
Once you’re ready to close the contract on Upwork, you’ll be asked to leave a review at that point — I’d be very grateful if you did!
Best wishes,
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
